topic: Sales per square foot by store size
decision: whether the next five stores should be large-format (over 38,000 sq ft) or standard size

columns.format: standard (under 33,000 sq ft) or large (over 38,000 sq ft)
columns.annual_sales_musd: sales in the last 12 months, $ millions
columns.sales_per_sqft_usd: annual sales per square foot, US dollars
columns.catchment_pop_k: people living within 15 minutes' drive, thousands

findings.text: Large stores sit in bigger catchments: 85,000 to 140,000 people within 15 minutes, against 30,000 to 90,000 for standard stores.
Large stores sell less per square foot: $469 a year on average, against $606 for standard stores.
Parking spaces rise with floor area (correlation 0.96).
The chain's top seller is S39 in Radley, a large store with $29.3 million in sales.
A large store averages $21.8 million in annual sales against $15.0 million for a standard store: 46% more sales for 88% more floor space.
Standard stores opened before 2010 sell about $19 more per square foot than newer standard stores.
Staff numbers track sales closely, at about 6 employees per $1 million of sales in both formats.
4 of the 11 large stores opened in 2025 or 2026 and are still building up trade. Without them, large stores average $514 per square foot, still below standard stores.
The average store has 29,950 square feet of selling space.
Two stores closed for six weeks of renovation; their sales are annualised.

main.gist: Bigger stores sell less per square foot; large format is a poor use of space

caveat.gist: Four large stores are new and still ramping up
